sections.name: File setup, limiter
sections.title: Setup and per-address limit
sections.what: Brings in the image and response helpers, the lab service, the limiter and the colour helper, and allows 30 requests per address per minute.
sections.why: Likely reason: the image is generated on the server, so requests are limited.
sections.watch_out: The limit is per address, so users on one network share it.

sections.name: GET
sections.title: Draw the called-it card
sections.what: Looks up the call's card, returns not-found if it is not graded, and draws the image with the title, confidence, moment, grade and calibration.
sections.why: The comment says a graded review never changes, which is the reason for the long cache.
sections.watch_out: The corrections approach in the AI page adds new records instead of editing, so a card cached for a day could show a replaced value.

summary: Draws the Called it share card for a graded call as a 1200 by 630 image, showing the display name, the title, the confidence and the grade.
purpose: Lets fans share a graded call as a picture.
why: The comment says a graded review never changes, so the image can be cached for a day.
how: 1) Limits requests per address to 30 per minute. 2) Looks up the card for the call id. 3) Returns not-found if the call is not graded. 4) Draws the image and returns it with a one-day immutable cache setting.
inputs: A GET with the call id in the address. Card data comes from the lab service.
outputs: A 1200 by 630 image, or a JSON error for rate limits and not-found.
risks: The one-day immutable cache assumes grades never change, so a corrected grade would stay wrong in caches for up to a day.
debug: If a card shows an old grade, check for a superseding correction and clear or wait out the cache. If a card is missing, check the call is graded.
